proofs.proof_tex:
Assign \(c(v)=1\) to every \(v\in V^{-}\).  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) identifies the
minimal residual clutter of \(G_H\) as
\[
 \mathcal C(G_H,s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E\bigr\}.
\]
Thus the constraint indexed by \(e=\{u,v\}\) is precisely
\[
 A\cap\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\neq\varnothing.
\]
Equivalently, by Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) and its hedge-hitting
identification bridge, these are exactly the interventions for which the
acquired proxy law identifies the causal target \(Q_s\).

Let \(C\subseteq U\) be a vertex cover of \(H\) and put
\[
 A_C=\{x_u:u\in C\}.
\]
For every \(e=\{u,v\}\in E\), at least one of \(u,v\) belongs to \(C\), so
\(A_C\) meets \(\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\).  Hence \(A_C\) is feasible and, because
all costs are one,
\[
 c(A_C)=\sum_{w\in A_C}c(w)=|C|.
\]
Minimizing over vertex covers gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)\leq\tau(H).
\]

Conversely, let \(A\subseteq V^{-}\) be any feasible intervention and begin
with
\[
 C_0=\{u\in U:x_u\in A\}.
\]
Process the edges in any fixed order.  Whenever an edge
\(e=\{u,v\}\) is not covered by the current set, insert one of its endpoints
(for definiteness, the \(\prec\)-smaller endpoint).  Feasibility implies
that \(z_e\in A\) whenever this insertion is required: indeed, neither
\(x_u\) nor \(x_v\) then belongs to \(A\), and the constraint
\(A\cap\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}\neq\varnothing\) forces \(z_e\in A\).  Associate the
insertion with this private guard.  Distinct processed edges have distinct
guards, and insertions that repeat an already inserted endpoint only reduce
the final cardinality.  The resulting set \(C_A\) covers every edge and
satisfies
\[
 |C_A|
 \leq |\{u:x_u\in A\}|+|\{e:z_e\in A\}|
 =|A|.
\]
The last equality uses the construction of \(G_H\), whose manipulable
vertices are exactly the source copies and private guards.  Applying this
map to an optimal intervention yields
\[
 \tau(H)\leq |C_A|\leq |A|=\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c).
\]
Together with the preceding upper bound, this proves
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)=\tau(H).
\]

We finally verify the approximation-preserving constants.  The forward map
\(H\mapsto G_H\) has
\(1+|U|+|E|\) vertices and is computable in polynomial time, and the reverse
replacement map just described is polynomial.  Equality of the optima gives
the first \(L\)-reduction inequality with \(\alpha=1\):
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)\leq \tau(H).
\]
Since every \(C_A\) is a vertex cover, \(|C_A|\geq\tau(H)\); combining this
with \(|C_A|\leq|A|\) and equality of the optima gives
\[
 0\leq |C_A|-\tau(H)
 \leq |A|-\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c),
\]
which is the second \(L\)-reduction inequality with \(\beta=1\).
Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}cubic\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}apx\mbox{-}complete}\)
states that Minimum Vertex Cover is \(\mathsf{APX}\)-complete, and hence
\(\mathsf{NP}\)-hard and \(\mathsf{APX}\)-hard, even when the source graph
has maximum degree at most three.  The unit-constant \(L\)-reduction
transfers both hardness conclusions.  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) supplies, for
every such source instance, residual rank three (when \(E\neq\varnothing\))
and a bidirected tree of radius at most two.  This proves every claimed
restriction.  If exact rank three rather than the promise \(r\leq3\) is
requested, edgeless source instances are recognized and solved trivially;
on every remaining instance \(E\neq\varnothing\), so the same reduction
has rank exactly three.

Fix the supplied total order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\).  Assumption
\(\mathrm{ass{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}promise}\) and Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}residual\mbox{-}rank}\) imply
\(|R|\leq3\) for every \(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\).  By Definitions
\(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\), each such
\(R\) equals \(F\setminus\{s\}\) for an inclusion-minimal hedge \(F\).
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) gives
\(|F|\geq4\), hence \(|R|\geq3\).  Therefore every clutter member has
exactly three vertices.  The final clause of the same theorem gives
\[
 R\subseteq P_s\cup T_s,\qquad
 R\cap P_s\neq\varnothing,\qquad
 R\cap T_s\neq\varnothing,\qquad
 P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing.
\]

The all-ones vector is feasible for the covering LP, so its feasible region
is nonempty.  It is a closed subset of the finite-dimensional compact cube
\([0,1]^{V^{-}}\); therefore its linear objective attains a minimum.
Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}promised\mbox{-}enumeration}\), instantiated
with \(r_0=3\) and \(\triangleleft_V\), lists all of its constraints in
polynomial time.  Because the coefficients and the positive costs are
rational, Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\)
returns an optimal rational solution \(y\).  Fix such a solution.

For \(0<t<1/2\), form \(A_t\) as in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\).  Suppose, toward a
contradiction, that \(A_t\cap R=\varnothing\) for some
\(R\in\mathcal C(G,s)\), and put \(a=|R\cap P_s|\).  The preceding
partition and \(|R|=3\) imply \(a\in\{1,2\}\).  Since \(R\) is missed, the
two threshold rules give the strict inequalities
\[
 y_p<t\quad(p\in R\cap P_s),
 \qquad
 y_b<\frac12-t\quad(b\in R\cap T_s).
\]
If \(a=1\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v
 <t+2\left(\frac12-t\right)=1-t<1;
\]
if \(a=2\), then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v
 <2t+\left(\frac12-t\right)=\frac12+t<1.
\]
Either conclusion contradicts the LP constraint
\(\sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1\).  Thus every \(A_t\) hits every member of the
minimal residual clutter.  Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\), through its cited hedge-hitting
bridge, now implies both that \(A_t\) is feasible and that the acquired
proxy law identifies \(Q_s\).

Let \(T\) be uniformly distributed on \((0,1/2)\); this auxiliary
randomization is used only to average deterministic threshold choices.  For
\(p\in P_s\), the event \(p\in A_T\) is \(T\leq y_p\), while for
\(b\in T_s\), the event \(b\in A_T\) is
\(T\geq1/2-y_b\).  Since \(0\leq y_v\leq1\), interval lengths give
\[
 \Pr(p\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_p\},
 \qquad
 \Pr(b\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y_b\}.
\]
No vertex outside \(P_s\cup T_s\) is selected.  Using
\(P_s\cap T_s=\varnothing\), linearity of expectation, and positivity of
the costs,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{v\in A_T}c(v)\right]
 &=\sum_{v\in P_s\cup T_s}c(v)\min\{1,2y_v\}\\
 &\leq2\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 =2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Every intervention feasible for Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) has an incidence vector feasible
for the covering LP with the same objective value.  Consequently
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]

Membership in \(A_t\) changes only at a value in
\[
 \{y_p:p\in P_s\}\cup
 \left\{\frac12-y_b:b\in T_s\right\}.
\]
The values in \((0,1/2)\) partition this interval into finitely many open
cells, and \(A_t\) is constant on every cell.  The critical values have
Lebesgue measure zero.  If each positive-length cell had cost strictly
larger than \(2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\), their finite weighted average
would have the same strict inequality, contradicting the expectation bound.
Thus some cell has cost at most \(2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\).  The optimal
basic vector \(y\) is rational, so every critical value is rational and a
rational representative of every nonempty cell is computable, for example
by taking the midpoint of its rational endpoints.  Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\) evaluates all these
representatives and all critical values; hence its cheapest output obeys
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)
 \leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]
There are at most \(2|V|\) critical values.  Enumerating the constraints,
solving the rational LP, sorting those values, and evaluating the candidates
are all polynomial-time operations.  The order used here is the supplied
causal-vertex order \(\triangleleft_V\), not the independent source order
\(\prec\) used in a private-guard expansion.  This proves the feasibility,
cost, and algorithmic assertions.

First consider any instance in the class of the theorem.  Choose
\(R_0\in\mathcal C(G,s)\), which is possible because the clutter is
nonempty.  Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\) imply
\(R_0\neq\varnothing\).  The stated positive-rational-cost condition and
finiteness give
\[
 m_0:=\min_{v\in R_0}c(v)>0.
\]
For any feasible LP vector \(y\), coordinatewise nonnegativity and the
constraint indexed by \(R_0\) imply
\[
 \sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v
 \geq\sum_{v\in R_0}c(v)y_v
 \geq m_0\sum_{v\in R_0}y_v
 \geq m_0>0.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)>0\), so the ratio in the theorem is well
defined.

Because \(V\) is finite, choose a total order \(\triangleleft_V\) on it and
supply this order to Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\mbox{-}three\mbox{-}rounding}\).  All of that
theorem's premises hold in the stated class, so it returns an identifying
intervention \(A_t\) with
\[
 \sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)\leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Since Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) minimizes over
all such interventions,
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq\sum_{v\in A_t}c(v)
 \leq2\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c).
\]
Division by the positive LP value proves the universal upper bound
\[
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)}{\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)}\leq2.
\]

For the matching lower bound, fix \(n\geq2\), give the source graph \(K_n\)
any total order \(\prec\) on \(U\), and form \(G_{K_n}\) by Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}expansion}\).  Assign unit cost
to every member of \(V^{-}\).  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) gives a finite
simple bow-free instance with a radius-at-most-two bidirected tree and
\[
 \mathcal C(G_{K_n},s)
 =\bigl\{\{x_u,x_v,z_e\}:e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\bigr\},
 \qquad r(G_{K_n},s)=3.
\]
Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\tau(K_n).
\]
Any set of at most \(n-2\) vertices of \(K_n\) omits two vertices and hence
misses their edge, whereas all but one vertex cover every edge.  Therefore
\(\tau(K_n)=n-1\).

For the LP, set \(y_{x_u}=1/2\) for every \(u\in U\) and \(y_{z_e}=0\) for
every \(e\in E(K_n)\).  Each clutter constraint then has left side one, so
this vector is feasible and has objective \(n/2\).  Conversely, sum the
constraints
\[
 y_{x_u}+y_{x_v}+y_{z_e}\geq1
\]
over all \(e=\{u,v\}\in E(K_n)\).  Each source copy occurs exactly \(n-1\)
times, and therefore
\[
 (n-1)\sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq\binom n2.
\]
Because \(n-1>0\), division gives
\[
 \sum_{u\in U}y_{x_u}
 +\frac1{n-1}\sum_{e\in E(K_n)}y_{z_e}
 \geq\frac n2.
\]
All coordinates are nonnegative and \(1/(n-1)\leq1\), so the unit-cost LP
objective is at least the left side of this display.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)=\frac n2,
 \qquad
 \frac{\operatorname{OPT}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
      {\operatorname{LP}(G_{K_n},s,c)}
 =\frac{n-1}{n/2}=2-\frac2n.
\]
For \(n=2\) the ratio is one, agreeing with the formula; as
\(n\to\infty\) the ratios tend to two.  Since these examples lie in the
class of the universal upper bound, its integrality-gap supremum is exactly
two.  Notice that the source order \(\prec\) used here is independent of the
causal-vertex order chosen only to invoke the rounding theorem.

Finally impose Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}unique\mbox{-}games}\), fix
\(\epsilon>0\), and suppose for contradiction that a polynomial-time
\((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation exists on the narrower subclass in the
statement.  Given a finite simple source graph \(H\) with at least one edge,
choose any source order, construct \(G_H\), and assign unit costs.  Theorem
\(\mathrm{thm{:}private\mbox{-}guard\mbox{-}realization}\) places the
resulting instance in that subclass.  If the hypothetical algorithm returns
a feasible intervention \(A\), the polynomial guard-replacement map from
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}objective\mbox{-}preserving\mbox{-}hardness}\)
returns a vertex cover \(C_A\) such that
\[
 |C_A|\leq|A|
 \leq(2-\epsilon)\operatorname{OPT}(G_H,s,c)
 =(2-\epsilon)\tau(H).
\]
For an edgeless \(H\), output the empty cover directly.  This would be a
polynomial-time \((2-\epsilon)\)-approximation for Minimum Vertex Cover on
all finite simple graphs, contradicting Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}ugc\mbox{-}vertex\mbox{-}cover\mbox{-}hardness}\).  The
claimed conditional lower bound follows.

Fix the supplied total order \(\triangleleft_V\) on \(V\), and introduce
the proof-local family
\[
 \mathcal C_{\leq3}
 =\{R\in\mathcal C(G,s):|R|\leq3\}.
\]
Apply Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}promised\mbox{-}enumerator}\), with input
\(\triangleleft_V\), to all \(R\subseteq V^{-}\) of size at most three.
The bidirected-connectivity and directed-reachability tests are exactly the
hedge conditions in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}singleton\mbox{-}hedges}\), and the proper-subset tests are
exactly the minimality condition in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}minimal\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}clutter}\).  Thus the output
is precisely \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), without duplicates and in the
lexicographic order induced by \(\triangleleft_V\).  This bounded
enumeration examines \(O(|V|^3)\) candidates and does not assume that the
global rank is at most three.

Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}first\mbox{-}rank\mbox{-}boundary}\) implies that
every member of \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\) has size exactly three, lies in the
disjoint union \(P_s\mathbin{\dot\cup}T_s\), and meets both parts.  Define
the restricted values
\[
 \operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}
 =\min\left\{\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y_v:
 y\in[0,1]^{V^{-}},
 \sum_{v\in R}y_v\geq1\ \text{for all }R\in\mathcal C_{\leq3}\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}
 =\min\left\{\sum_{v\in A}c(v):
 A\subseteq V^{-},
 A\cap R\neq\varnothing\ \text{for all }R\in\mathcal C_{\leq3}\right\}.
\]
These are local names for the bounded-obstruction relaxation and do not
alter the global definitions.

The restricted LP has rational data and a nonempty compact feasible region.
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}rational\mbox{-}lp\mbox{-}polynomial\mbox{-}time}\)
therefore returns an optimal rational solution \(y^{(3)}\) in polynomial
time.  For \(0<t<1/2\), apply the parent-spouse threshold formula to
\(y^{(3)}\).  If the resulting \(A_t\) missed a member of
\(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\) having one parent, then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y^{(3)}_v
 <t+2\left(\frac12-t\right)=1-t<1;
\]
if it missed one having two parents, then
\[
 \sum_{v\in R}y^{(3)}_v
 <2t+\left(\frac12-t\right)=\frac12+t<1.
\]
Both conclusions contradict the corresponding restricted LP constraint.
Thus every threshold set hits \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\).

For an auxiliary \(T\) uniform on \((0,1/2)\), the interval-length
calculation gives
\[
 \Pr(p\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y^{(3)}_p\},
 \qquad
 \Pr(b\in A_T)=\min\{1,2y^{(3)}_b\}.
\]
Using positivity of \(c\), disjointness of \(P_s\) and \(T_s\), and
linearity of expectation,
\[
 \mathbb E[c(A_T)]
 \leq2\sum_{v\in V^{-}}c(v)y^{(3)}_v
 =2\operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}.
\]
The finite rational-breakpoint argument in Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}parent\mbox{-}spouse\mbox{-}rounding}\) therefore returns
an evaluated set \(A^{\mathrm{rnd}}\) satisfying
\[
 c(A^{\mathrm{rnd}})\leq2\operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}.
\]
Every globally feasible intervention hits \(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), so its
incidence vector is feasible for the restricted LP.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{LP}_{\leq3}\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c),
 \qquad
 c(A^{\mathrm{rnd}})\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c).
\]
Alternatively, an exact optimization backend may return an integral
minimizer \(A^{(3)}\) of the restricted family, with
\(c(A^{(3)})=\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}\).  This alternative asserts no
polynomial running time for exact integral optimization.

For either returned set \(A\), apply Lemma
\(\mathrm{lem{:}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}hedge\mbox{-}oracle}\) to
\(F_0=V\setminus A\).  Because \(A\subseteq V^{-}\), one has \(s\in F_0\).
The lemma says that alternating restriction to directed ancestors of \(s\)
and to the bidirected component of \(s\) terminates at \(\{s\}\) if and
only if \(F_0\) contains no hedge.  Since the graph is finite, every hedge
contains an inclusion-minimal hedge.  Therefore successful termination is
equivalent to \(A\) hitting all of \(\mathcal C(G,s)\), which by Definition
\(\mathrm{def{:}mcid\mbox{-}objective}\) is equivalent to global
feasibility and identification of \(Q_s\) from the acquired proxy law.

If \(A=A^{(3)}\) and verification succeeds, restriction of the constraint
family gives
\(\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}\leq\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\), whereas
global feasibility gives
\[
 \operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)
 \leq c(A^{(3)})=\operatorname{OPT}_{\leq3}.
\]
Thus equality holds and the exact restricted optimum is globally exact.  If
\(A=A^{\mathrm{rnd}}\) and verification succeeds, the already proved bound
\(c(A^{\mathrm{rnd}})\leq2\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\) certifies the global
factor-two guarantee.

Suppose instead that verification fails.  The fixed-point oracle returns a
hedge \(F\subseteq V\setminus A\).  For each
\(v\in F\setminus\{s\}\), run the oracle on \(F\setminus\{v\}\).  Whenever
a hedge survives, replace \(F\) by the fixed-point hedge returned by that
call and restart the scan.  Every replacement strictly decreases \(|F|\),
so there are at most \(|V|-1\) replacements and at most \(|V|-1\) oracle
calls between replacements.  The deletion procedure is consequently
polynomial-time.

At termination, no \(F\setminus\{v\}\), for
\(v\in F\setminus\{s\}\), contains a hedge.  If a proper hedge
\(J\subsetneq F\) existed, both hedges would contain \(s\), so some
\(v\in F\setminus J\) would differ from \(s\); then
\(J\subseteq F\setminus\{v\}\), a contradiction.  Hence \(F\) is
inclusion-minimal, and
\[
 R:=F\setminus\{s\}\in\mathcal C(G,s).
\]
Also \(F\subseteq V\setminus A\) implies \(A\cap R=\varnothing\).  Both
\(A^{(3)}\) and \(A^{\mathrm{rnd}}\) hit every member of
\(\mathcal C_{\leq3}\), so this missed residual is not in that family and
\(|R|>3\).  The final induced graph directly verifies connectivity and
reachability, while the unsuccessful single-deletion oracle calls verify
minimality.  Thus the procedure returns the claimed verifiable rank
violation.
